result:
Staging this from outcomes. Here are the spec's requirements recast as outcome candidates. They are unranked and need your ranking before I name any stages or write roadmap text.

## Outcome candidates

| # | Outcome (what you get) | Spec | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | A Parquet filing-index catalog for a chosen range of archived quarters, built from saved original index files | R1, R3, R5; §2.1 Backfill, §4.2, §4.4, §4.6 | About 2 SEC requests per quarter (directory listing plus `master.idx`), so requests are minutes at 3 req/s. Bytes per quarter are unknown to me, see probe below. The range is unset (§4.8 assumes no start year). Your time grows with range width, because §4.6 needs golden fixtures for every historical format in the range. |
| O2 | Daily indexes added to that catalog on an ongoing basis, catching up after missed runs and across quarter boundaries | R2, R5; §4.2 Daily | About 1 file per business day, roughly 250 a year, plus catch-up from the handoff date. Negligible next to O1. |
| O3 | A rebuild of the catalog from saved files after a parser change, with no new SEC downloads | R6; §4.5, §4.6 | No SEC traffic. Compute is measured when run. |
| O4 | Weekly reconciliation that records additions and changed fields, and holds removals until you approve them against the exact source hash | R7, R10; §4.4 | Re-downloads every supported quarter weekly: quarters × bytes per quarter, the same unknown as O1. Your time is needed for each withdrawal approval. |
| O5 | All SEC traffic from every run under one shared, identified request budget | R8, R11; §4.3, §4.8 | No direct cost. The target is 3 req/s against the SEC's published 10 req/s ceiling. |
| O6 | Readers see only complete quarter versions through one active pointer, and a failed run leaves the previous version readable | R9; §4.5, §4.6 | Storage grows with each retained generation. Retention is unset (§4.8). |
| O7 | The pipelines running unattended in your Azure subscription, with schedules, alerts, runbooks and rollback | R4; §4.1, §4.7, §4.9, §7 | Azure cost depends on region, job sizes and retention, which §4.8 leaves to implementation, so it can only be measured when run. Your time goes to the subscription, identities and role assignments. |

R5 (shared code) and R11 (stated defaults) are constraints across several outcomes, so I cited them rather than listing them as outcomes of their own.

Qualities to place when the roadmap is written: source manifests, traceability, full validation suite.

**Probe offer.** To firm up the byte-volume notes for O1 and O4, I can fetch the SEC `full-index` listing for one recent and one old quarter and read their file sizes. That is two or three requests with an identified User-Agent. I'll run it only if you say yes.

## Proposed tracks

- **Track A: Filing-index catalog** (O1–O6), known progression. The spec's design fixes the method, including the withdrawal policy and publication contract.
- **Track B: Azure operation** (O7), known progression. I've proposed this kind, but the ADR is still *Proposed*, and §9 keeps a schedule-only container alternative open. If you consider the platform undecided, I'd call this track research instead.
  - **Why split:** the catalog's correctness can be checked locally, on fixtures and real files, without any Azure resource. Whether it runs unattended in your subscription is a different use, an operational one. B needs A's code, but A's answer stands without B.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14 (`.python-version`), in a uv workspace.
- Azure services per the ADR: ADF, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS Gen2, Table Storage, Azure Monitor. The ADR's status is Proposed.
- Output in Parquet; SEC request target of 3 req/s.
- Code location: §4.9 names `packages/sec-edgar-ingest`. The repository also has `sec-edgar-client`, `sec-edgar-download` and `sec-edgar-index-ingest` scaffolds, which the spec doesn't mention.

The roadmap will be `specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md`, named from the spec's stem.

**Your call:** please rank the outcomes within each track and the two tracks against each other. Also confirm or change the tracks and their kinds, correcting any choice above while you're at it (notably which package the code goes in), and say whether to run the probe.
